overview: This is VIZIO Holding Corp.'s amended response to the amended complaint filed by BH Innovations LLC, Longitude Licensing Limited, and 138 East LCD Advancements Ltd. in Section 337 investigation 337-TA-1462 concerning liquid crystal display devices, components, and products containing them. VIZIO denies infringement of the asserted patents (U.S. Patent Nos. 7,705,948 and 7,570,334), asserts multiple affirmative defenses including non-infringement and invalidity, and denies that a domestic industry exists in the United States.

points.point: VIZIO Holding Corp., located at 39 Tesla, Irvine, California 92618, is the respondent in this investigation and denies that it has violated Section 337 or the Tariff Act of 1930.
points.quote: RESPONDENT VIZIO HOLDING CORP.'S AMENDED RESPONSE TO THE AMENDED COMPLAINT OF BH INNOVATIONS LLC

points.point: Complainants are BH Innovations LLC (BHI), Longitude Licensing Limited (Longitude), and 138 East LCD Advancements Ltd. (138).
points.quote: filed by BH Innovations LLC ("BHI"), Longitude Licensing Limited ("Longitude") and 138 East LCD Advancements Ltd. ("138")

points.point: LCD devices comprise liquid crystal material sandwiched between two layers called substrates; LCD devices use optical and electrical properties of liquid crystal molecules to control light transmission through pixels controlled by thin-film transistors.
points.quote: LCD device may comprise a liquid crystal material that is sandwiched between two layers known as substrates

points.point: The investigation concerns liquid crystal display devices, components thereof, and products containing the same, specifically LCD devices such as television screens and computer monitors.
points.quote: complained of alleged unfair importation into the United States, sale for importation into the United States, and/or sale within the United States after importation of certain liquid crystal display ("LCD") devices

points.point: VIZIO denies all allegations of the complaint except as expressly admitted, denies any characterizations of the Asserted Patents not disclosed therein, and denies that it has infringed the Asserted Patents or committed any unfair methods of competition or unfair acts.
points.quote: VIZIO denies any unfair methods of competition or unfair acts

points.point: VIZIO challenges that Complainants have established a domestic industry, alleging that Complainants fail to demonstrate that Innolux has made significant investments in plant and equipment, significant employment of labor and capital, and/or substantial investments in exploitation of the Asserted Patents.
points.quote: Complainants fail to demonstrate that Innolux has made significant investments in plant and equipment, significant employment of labor and capital

points.point: VIZIO asserts that it does not directly infringe, indirectly infringe, contribute to infringement, or induce infringement of any valid or enforceable claim of the Asserted Patents, either literally or under the doctrine of equivalents.
points.quote: VIZIO does not directly infringe, indirectly infringe, contribute to infringement, or induce infringement of any valid or enforceable claim

points.point: VIZIO alleges that all asserted claims of the Asserted Patents are invalid under 35 U.S.C. §§ 101, 102, 103, 112, 116, and/or 256, and are invalid under 35 U.S.C. § 102 and/or § 103 in view of prior art identified on the face of the asserted patents and in their prosecution histories.
points.quote: asserted claims of the Asserted Patents are invalid under 35 U.S.C. § 102 and/or 35 U.S.C. § 103 in view of at least the prior art identified on the face

points.point: VIZIO alleges that the '334 patent is unenforceable for inequitable conduct because the named inventor Masao Murade intentionally withheld material prior art references during prosecution with specific intent to deceive the Examiner regarding claim 14's patentability.
points.quote: the '334 patent is unenforceable for inequitable conduct, because during prosecution the named inventor of the '334 patent, Masao Murade, intentionally withheld information material to the patentability

points.point: VIZIO alleges that the named inventor Masao Murade withheld material prior art references including U.S. Patent App. Pub. No. 2005/0078240 (later issued as U.S. Patent No. 7,196,353), U.S. Patent No. 6,433,841, U.S. Patent No. 6,611,301, and U.S. Patent No. 6,897,932, all listing him as a named inventor and disclosing 'dummy pixel' subject matter.
points.quote: U.S. Patent App. Pub. No. 2005/0078240 (later issued as U.S. Patent No. 7,196,353); U.S. Patent No. 6,433,841; U.S. Patent No. 6,611,301; and U.S. Patent No. 6,897,932

points.point: VIZIO asserts prosecution history estoppel, alleging that due to admissions and statements made to the USPTO during prosecution of the Asserted Patents, Complainants are estopped from construing a valid and enforceable claim as infringed literally or under the doctrine of equivalents.
points.quote: due to admissions and statements made to the United States Patent and Trademark Office during the prosecution of the applications that resulted in the Asserted Patents

points.point: VIZIO asserts patent exhaustion, license, and/or implied license as defenses, alleging that Complainants' claims against VIZIO are barred as a result of patent exhaustion, a license, and/or an implied license to the Asserted Patents.
points.quote: Complainants' claims against VIZIO are barred as a result of patent exhaustion, a license, and/or an implied license to the Asserted Patents

points.point: VIZIO asserts the doctrine of ensnarement, alleging that Complainants' claims are barred to the extent they make infringement claims under the doctrine of equivalents that would ensnare prior art.
points.quote: Complainants' claims are barred by the doctrine of ensnarement to the extent that Complainants make infringement claims under the doctrine of equivalents

points.point: VIZIO asserts prosecution laches as a defense, alleging that Complainants have prejudiced VIZIO by inexcusably delaying prosecution of applications for the Asserted Patents.
points.quote: Complainants' claims are barred by the doctrine of prosecution laches because Complainants have prejudiced VIZIO by inexcusably delaying prosecution

points.point: VIZIO asserts laches, acquiescence, and waiver, alleging that Complainants have known of the Accused Products of VIZIO for several years and their delay in pursuing any valid right or claim has prejudiced VIZIO and precludes the relief Complainants seek.
points.quote: On information and belief, Complainants have known of the Accused Products of VIZIO for several years

points.point: VIZIO asserts improper inventorship as a defense, reserving the right to assert that any Asserted Patent fails to name the appropriate inventors.
points.quote: To the extent that VIZIO determines through discovery and investigation that any Asserted Patent fails to name the appropriate inventors

points.point: VIZIO asserts lack of statutory authority as a defense, alleging that one or more Complainants lacks substantial rights in the Asserted Patents due to the existence of multiple tortured license agreements that preclude Complainants from claiming substantial rights and therefore lack standing.
points.quote: Complainants have extremely narrow rights due to the existence of multiple tortured license agreements that preclude Complainants from claiming substantial rights

points.point: VIZIO asserts that at least some of the Accused Products are covered by one or more license agreements to one or more respondents.
points.quote: At least some of the Accused Products are covered by one or more license agreements to one or more respondents

points.point: VIZIO denies that Complainants are entitled to any relief requested, including an exclusion order, cease and desist order, or any other form of relief, and argues that granting such relief would not be consistent with the Public Interest under 19 U.S.C. § 1337(d)(1).
points.quote: the requested relief should not issue because of its potential adverse effects upon the public health and welfare, competitive conditions in the United States economy

points.point: VIZIO asserts lack of importation as a defense, reserving the right to argue that Complainants cannot prove that the allegedly infringing articles are imported into the United States, sold for importation into the United States, or sold after importation into the United States by VIZIO.
points.quote: To the extent that Complainants are unable to prove that the allegedly infringing articles are imported into the United States, sold for importation into the United States, or sold after importation

points.point: VIZIO denies that it has committed any unfair methods of competition or unfair acts in violation of Section 337 of the Tariff Act of 1930.
points.quote: VIZIO denies that any such assertion is correct or proper and, in particular, VIZIO denies that they infringe any of the Asserted Patents and denies that they have committed any unfair methods of competition and unfair acts

points.point: VIZIO denies any characterizations of the Asserted Patents to the extent they purport to attribute to the Asserted Patents anything not covered by the scope of the Asserted Patents.
points.quote: VIZIO denies any characterizations relating to the Asserted Patents to the extent they purport to attribute to the Asserted Patents anything that is not covered by the scope of the Asserted Patents

points.point: VIZIO states that it has not fully collected and reviewed all information relevant to the matters and issues raised, and reserves the right to seek amendment of, modify, and/or expand its defenses and to take further positions as discovery proceeds in this investigation.
points.quote: Discovery is ongoing as of the time of this Response and thus VIZIO has not fully collected and reviewed all of the information that may be relevant

points.point: VIZIO admits that from January 2025 to November 2025, it imported VIZIO LCD models containing the accused HKC panel, with VIZIO, Inc. being an importer of record for such shipments under HTS number 8528.72.6430.
points.quote: from January 2025 to November 2025, the quantity and value of the VIZIO LCD models containing the accused HKC panel imported by VIZIO were approximately

points.point: The Accused Products consist of VIZIO LCD models containing accused HKC panels, imported and sold by VIZIO, with manufacturing capacity and sales information provided in the filing.
points.quote: VIZIO's manufacturing capacity is fully dependent on

points.point: VIZIO admits that Complainants purport to have filed a Complaint pursuant to Section 337 of the Tariff Act of 1930 alleging unfair importation and sale of LCD devices and components, and that Complainants purport to assert the '948 and '334 patents claiming infringement of claim 1.
points.quote: VIZIO admits that the Complaint purports to assert infringement of claim 1 of the Asserted Patents

points.point: VIZIO admits that the Commission has instituted an investigation as set forth in the Notice of Investigation dated November 24, 2025 and published in the Federal Register on November 28, 2025, but denies that it is in violation of 19 U.S.C. § 1337.
points.quote: VIZIO acknowledges that the Commission has instituted an investigation as set forth in the Commission's Notice of Investigation, dated November 24, 2025

points.point: VIZIO lacks sufficient information and knowledge to form a belief as to whether Complainants meet the domestic industry requirement and denies such allegations on that basis.
points.quote: VIZIO lacks sufficient information and knowledge to form a belief as to the truth of Complainants' allegation that they meet the domestic industry requirement

points.point: VIZIO requests that the Commission deny all relief Complainants requested, determine that VIZIO has not violated Section 337, has not infringed the Asserted Patents, find that the asserted claims are invalid and that the '334 patent is unenforceable, find no domestic industry exists, and award VIZIO its attorneys' fees and costs.
points.quote: Determining that VIZIO has not violated Section 337 of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended, 19 U.S.C. § 1337

rejected.point: Complainants assert U.S. Patent No. 7,705,948 (the '948 patent) and U.S. Patent No. 7,570,334 (the '334 patent), with focus on claim 1 of the Asserted Patents.
rejected.quote: U.S. Patent No. 7,705,948 (the "'948 patent") and U.S. Patent No. 7,570,334 (the "'334 patent")
